unmapped_findings: The product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation (UTS × TE) of the as-cast 6Cr steel strip is 38.0 GPa %, the highest among all the studied strips (Table 2).
Measured lattice parameter of the κ-carbides and γ-austenite in the as-cast 6Cr steel strip is 0.389 nm and 0.384 nm, respectively.

The yield strength of the as-cast 6Cr steel strip (718 MPa) is higher than that of the as-cast 3Cr steel strip (642 MPa), attributed to solid solution strengthening caused by the higher Cr content, because precipitation strengthening is low in both as-cast 3Cr and 6Cr strips due to the small κ-carbide volume fraction.

The strain hardening rate of the two as-cast Cr-containing steel strips (including 6Cr) gradually decreases during deformation; the 'hump' present in the strain hardening rate curve of the Cr-free steel becomes weak with Cr addition.
The DO3 phase size in the as-cast 6Cr strip (28 ± 4 nm) shows no significant change compared with the as-cast 3Cr strip (30 ± 3 nm).
Nominal composition of the alloy is Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-6Cr (wt. %); measured composition (Table 1): Mn 20.18, Al 9.12, C 1.20, Cr 6.08, S 0.0011, Fe Bal. (wt. %).
